RECALLWEAVE · LINEAR ALGEBRA LAB

When a transformation stays on a line

Apply a matrix. Follow a vector. Find the directions that stretch, reverse or vanish without leaving their line through the origin.

Show approximate eigenline drawings

Equal axis scale: each grid interval is 1. Tiny vectors use an endpoint dot. There are two real eigenlines. Eigenline geometry is approximate.

Integer probes allow an exact yes/no check. A drawing uses rounded coordinates: looking nearly aligned is not the same as satisfying Av = λv.

Exact check for this probe
(2)×(2) − (1)×(3) = 1 ≠ 0 → not collinear

For a nonzero input v = (x, y) and output Av = (u, w), the two vectors are collinear exactly when xw − yu = 0. This test includes a zero output.

Read the equation carefully

Av = λv, with v ≠ 0

The line is preserved. The arrow may keep its direction, reverse it, or collapse to the origin. The zero vector is never an eigenvector.

Why repeated roots need another check

The model covers real 2×2 integer matrices within the displayed bounds. Its integer probes cannot exactly represent an irrational slope. Complex eigenvalues are reported symbolically; their eigenvectors are outside this real-plane drawing.

Original examples and wording. Mathematical references: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.06SC and MIT 18.06, Lecture 21. Sources are optional reading; the lab works offline.
